title: Finite graded modules flat over a local coefficient ring are finitely presented
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a nonzero commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal. Let $n\geq0$ and let $w_1,\ldots,w_n$ be positive integers. Give $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] the grading in which $R$ has degree $0$ and $x_i$ has degree $w_i$: $P_d$ is the $R$-span of monomials $x^\alpha$ with $\sum_iw_i\alpha_i=d$ (and $P_d=0$ for $d<0$). Let $L$ be a $P$-module with an internal grading $L=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbf Z}L_d$ by $R$-submodules satisfying $P_eL_d\subseteq L_{e+d}$. If $L$ is finite as a $P$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $L$ is finitely presented as a $P$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Tag 053C, lemma-flat-graded-finite-type-finite-presentation-module, statement at lines 5856--5870 and proof at lines 5873--5909

proof.text: Choose finitely many homogeneous generators m_i by replacing a finite generating family with the components of its internal direct-sum decomposition. Let δ_i be their degrees, F = P^I with shifted pieces F_d = ∏_i P_(d-δ_i), and f:F→L their linear-combination surjection. Positivity of the weights bounds the monomials in each polynomial piece, so each F_d is finite over R. Weighted homogeneous projections give an internal decomposition of F; f preserves degree, commutes with projections, and induces surjections f_d:F_d→L_d. The same projections restrict to K=ker f and give K its internal grading.

source.place: Tag 053C, first paragraph of proof, lines 5873--5886

proof.text: The R-span of products P_(d-δ_i)m_i equals L_d, by applying the degree-d projection to polynomial linear combinations of the homogeneous generators. Hence L_d is finite over R. Its inclusion into L has its degree projection as retraction, so it is flat by lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-retract, and free by lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free. A finite free module is finitely presented. Since F_d is finite, the kernel of the surjection f_d:F_d→L_d is finite (Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker). Identify it with K_d by the evident linear equivalence. No flatness or freeness of K_d is required.

Put κ=R/𝔪. Flatness of L and lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective make K⊗_Rκ→F⊗_Rκ injective. The finite-type κ-algebra κ⊗_R P is Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian; the commutativity equivalence gives the same for P⊗_Rκ. The map P→P⊗_Rκ is surjective. Restriction of scalars along this surjection preserves Noetherianity, so F⊗_Rκ≅(P⊗_Rκ)^I is Noetherian over P. Its submodule K⊗_Rκ is therefore finite by lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite. Lift a finite generating family through the surjection q:K→K⊗_Rκ, x↦x⊗1. Replacing each lift by its finitely many homogeneous components gives a finite homogeneous set s⊂K whose P-span N still maps onto K⊗_Rκ.

The P-span N of the homogeneous set s is stable under every degree projection: decompose polynomial coefficients and retain only terms of complementary degree. For a∈K_d, surjectivity of q(N) gives b∈N with b⊗1=a⊗1. Applying the tensor of the degree-d projection gives π_d(b)⊗1=a⊗1 with π_d(b)∈N∩K_d. Thus N∩K_d maps onto κ⊗_R K_d. Since K_d is finite, lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators shows N∩K_d=K_d. Summing the finitely supported homogeneous decomposition of each element gives N=K. Hence K is finitely generated, and Module.finitePresentation_of_free_of_surjective applied to f gives the required finite presentation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 053C, proof lines 5873--5909; K9 formalization replaces the unnecessary freeness of K_d by Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker and uses degree projections to lift residue generators.
